context.title: Esperet et al.'s flow reconfiguration equivalence conjecture
context.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and $k$ a positive integer. A **$k$-flow** is a nowhere-zero integer flow with $0<|f(e)|<k$ on every edge, and an **$A$-flow** is a nowhere-zero flow with values in an abelian group $A$. Let $\mathcal{F}(G,k)$ and $\mathcal{F}(G,\mathbb{Z}_k)$ be the reconfiguration graphs whose vertices are the corresponding flows and whose edges represent flow-adjacency.

**Esperet et al.'s flow reconfiguration conjecture.** For each graph $G$ and each positive integer $k$,

$$
\mathcal{F}(G,k)\text{ is connected if and only if }\mathcal{F}(G,\mathbb{Z}_k)\text{ is connected}.
$$

One direction is easy, since reducing flow values modulo $k$ maps walks to walks. The reverse direction remains open; the source also gives examples showing that reconfiguration can distinguish nonisomorphic groups of the same order.
context.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston, Jiaao Li, Bo Su, Zhouningxin Wang and Ningyan Xu, “Reconfiguration of Nowhere-zero Flows”, arXiv:2606.24685 (2026).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24685

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2026). “Despite some beautiful partial results , all $3$ conjectures remain open.”

context.title: The regular oriented graph Hamilton decomposition conjecture above the $3/8$ threshold
context.statement: For $\gamma>0$, let $n_0=n_0(\gamma)$ be a threshold. An **$r$-regular oriented graph** on $n$ vertices is an oriented graph in which every vertex has indegree and outdegree $r$. **The conjecture.** For every $\gamma>0$ there exists $n_0=n_0(\gamma)$ such that, for all $n\geq n_0$ and all $r\geq(3/8+\gamma)n$, every $r$-regular oriented graph on $n$ vertices has a decomposition into Hamilton cycles. This would significantly generalize Kelly's conjecture. The source proves an approximate result for almost-regular oriented graphs with semidegree above $(3/8+\gamma)n$, while the exact decomposition statement remains open there.
context.source_name: Daniela Kühn, Deryk Osthus and Andrew Treglown, “Hamilton decompositions of regular tournaments”, arXiv:0908.3411 (2009).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0908.3411

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2009).

context.title: Threshold existence conjecture for graph sequences
context.statement: Let ${\cal G}=\{G_1,\ldots,G_n,\ldots\}$ be a graph sequence, and let $th({\cal G})$ denote its threshold when one exists. **Threshold existence conjecture.** Every graph sequence ${\cal G}$ has a threshold $th({\cal G})$. The conjecture concerns the missing general existence theorem for pebbling thresholds; the supplied status evidence says this implication is false.

context.title: The crosspolytopal peg conjecture
context.statement: Let $d\geq 2$, and let $\gamma:S^{d-1}\to\mathbbm{R}^d$ be a smooth embedding of the $(d-1)$-sphere into $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. A **regular $d$-dimensional cross-polytope** is the convex hull of $d$ mutually orthogonal pairs of opposite vertices at equal distance from the center. **Crosspolytopal peg conjecture.** Every smooth embedding $\gamma:S^{d-1}\to\mathbbm{R}^d$ contains the vertices of a regular $d$-dimensional cross-polytope. Guggenheimer proved this claim, but an error in his main lemma appears to invalidate the proof, leaving the problem open.
context.source_name: Benjamin Matschke, “On the Square Peg Problem and Its Relatives”, arXiv:1001.0186 (2022).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.0186

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2010).

context.title: Addario-Berry–Havet–Linhares Sales–Thomassé–Reed antidirected tree conjecture
context.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer.

**Addario-Berry–Havet–Linhares Sales–Thomassé–Reed conjecture.** If

$$
e(D)\geq (k-1)|V(D)|,
$$

then $D$ contains a copy of every antidirected tree with $k$ edges.

This is a directed analogue of the Erdős–Sós conjecture. The source introduces it as an open generalization for directed graphs.
context.source_name: Alexey Pokrovskiy, “Hyperstability in the Erdős-Sós Conjecture”, arXiv:2409.15191 (2024).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15191

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

context.title: Burr–Erdős linear Ramsey conjecture for bounded-degree graphs
context.literal_statement: Let $\Delta\in\mathbb{N}$. A graph has **bounded maximum degree** at most $\Delta$ when $\Delta(G)\leq\Delta$. **Burr–Erdős conjecture.** There exists $c=c(\Delta)>0$ such that every $2$-edge-colored $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of every graph $G$ with at most $cn$ vertices and $\Delta(G)\leq\Delta$. This is a foundational linear Ramsey-number conjecture for sparse graphs; the supplied source does not indicate whether this formulation is resolved.

context.title: Approximate Seymour second neighbourhood conjecture
context.statement:
Let $G$ be an oriented graph, and let $N^+_1(G,v)$ and $N^+_2(G,v)$ denote the first and second out-neighbourhoods of $v$.

**Approximate Seymour conjecture.** For every $epsilon>0$, every oriented graph $G$ has at least one vertex $v$ satisfying

$$
|N^+_2(G,v)| \geq (1-\epsilon)|N^+_1(G,v)|.
$$

The paper states this as an equivalent reformulation of Seymour's second neighbourhood conjecture, obtained using lexicographic products; it remains open together with the original conjecture.

context.title: Classification conjecture for Seymour Cayley orientations
context.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and let a **Seymour Cayley orientation** mean a Cayley orientation in which every vertex has equally large first and second out-neighbourhoods.

**Cayley classification conjecture.** Every Seymour Cayley orientation can be constructed by taking, possibly repeatedly, lexicographic products of empty graphs, powers of directed cycles, and regular tournaments.

The paper proves this classification for Cayley orientations of abelian groups. The conjecture asks whether the same description holds for Seymour Cayley orientations over arbitrary groups.

context.title: Distance-transitive Seymour-tight orientation conjecture
context.statement:
A **Seymour-tight orientation** is an orientation $G$ in which every vertex $v$ satisfies $|N^+_2(G,v)|=|N^+_1(G,v)|$. A digraph is **distance-transitive** when its automorphism group is transitive on ordered pairs of vertices at each fixed directed distance.

**Distance-transitive Seymour-tightness conjecture.** Every distance-transitive digraph is a Seymour-tight orientation.

Directed cycles, Paley tournaments, and certain lexicographic products provide known distance-transitive Seymour-tight examples. The proposed conjecture seeks a complete structural property for all distance-transitive digraphs and remains open.

context.title: Ramsey-cofinite versus Ramsey-lower-dense conjecture

literal.statement: Let $G$ be a graph. A graph is **Ramsey-cofinite** when it has the cofinite monochromatic embedding property defined in the paper, and it is **Ramsey-lower-dense** when it has positive Ramsey lower density in the paper's terminology. **Ramsey-cofinite conjecture.** If $G$ is not Ramsey-cofinite, then $G$ is not Ramsey-lower-dense. The source says this is suspected for every graph and relates it to a weaker previously asked question; no resolution is given.

context.title: Ulam reconstruction conjecture for infinite graphs with non-isomorphic vertex-deleted subgraphs
context.literal_statement:
Let $G$) be an infinite graph with vertex set $E$. For $x\in E$, write $G|E\setminus\{x\}$ for the subgraph induced by deleting $x$, and write $\sim$ for graph isomorphism. **Ulam reconstruction conjecture.** If

$$
\forall x \in E,\quad G|E\setminus\{x\}\nsim G|E,
$$

then $G$ is Ulam-reconstructible. This is one of several proposed sufficient conditions for reconstructibility of infinite graphs; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been proved or disproved.

context.title: Ulam reconstruction conjecture from pairwise isomorphic vertex-deleted subgraphs

literal.statement:
Let $G$ be an infinite graph with vertex set $E$. For distinct vertices $x,y\in E$, write $G|E\setminus\{x\}$ for the subgraph induced by deleting $x$, and write $\sim$ for graph isomorphism. **Ulam reconstruction conjecture.** If

$$
\forall (x,y)\in E^2,\quad x\neq y;\quad G|E\setminus\{x\}\sim G|E\setminus\{y\},
$$

then $G$ is Ulam-reconstructible. The source presents this as a conjectural sufficient condition for infinite-graph reconstruction, with no supplied resolution.

context.title: Ulam reconstruction conjecture from pairwise isomorphic vertex-deleted subgraphs

literal.statement:
Let $G$ be an infinite graph with vertex set $E$. For distinct vertices $x,y\in E$, write $G|E\setminus\{x\}$ for the subgraph induced by deleting $x$, and write $\sim$ for graph isomorphism. **Ulam reconstruction conjecture.** If

$$
\forall (x,y)\in E^2,\quad x\neq y;\quad G|E\setminus\{x\}\sim G|E\setminus\{y\},
$$

then $G$ is Ulam-reconstructible. The source presents this as a conjectural sufficient condition for infinite-graph reconstruction, with no supplied resolution.
